artists.biography: Todd Harry Rundgren (born June 22, 1948) is an American multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and record producer. Hailed in the early stage of his career as a new pop star, supported by the certified gold solo double LP Something/Anything? in 1972, his career has produced a diverse range of recordings as solo artist, and during the seventies and eighties with the band Utopia. He has also been prolific as a producer and engineer on the recorded work of other musicians.

perplexity.description:
Todd Rundgren's Initiation, released in 1975 on Bearsville Records, stands as a bold and ambitious entry in his eclectic discography. The album is notable for its fusion of electronic and rock elements, showcasing Rundgren's pioneering use of synthesizers and experimental production techniques. At over an hour in length, Initiation was the longest single album ever released at the time, reflecting Rundgren's desire to push the boundaries of the LP format. The music ranges from lush, synth-driven soundscapes to more traditional rock arrangements, with tracks like "Real Man" and "Initiation" highlighting his blend of pop sensibility and avant-garde exploration.

Within Rundgren's catalog, Initiation marks a transitional period where his interest in electronic music began to take center stage, foreshadowing his later work with Utopia and his reputation as a studio innovator. The album's ambitious scope and genre-blurring approach set it apart from his earlier, more straightforward rock efforts. While Initiation did not achieve major commercial success, it was critically noted for its technical ambition and creative risks, cementing Rundgren's status as a forward-thinking artist unafraid to challenge musical conventions.
